The calibration search on the sraffian arm — the fit trajectory, and why fit is not stability

Seed 20260923, the full 500-draw run: the objective falls 0.809 → 0.0294 and then plateaus, while the debt bound that would make the baseline stable is never the thing being minimised.

Read from: the live stderr trace of the detached search (/tmp/calib_search_gdp.log), parsed into qmd/reports/2026-09-27-calibration-search-evidence/trail.csv. The search itself is R/calibrate_random_search.R --arm sraffian --iters 500 --scale gdp --deflate --period 100 (default instruments: taxes, propensities, markups).

Status of claims: every number below is recomputed in this document’s setup chunk from the parsed trace; nothing is typed by hand. The search ran to completion (500 draws, 11 accepted).

1. What is being minimised — and what is not

The scalar the search minimises is calib_fitness with scale = "gdp", deflate = TRUE, scored at period = 100: the mean squared deviation of the 24 target cells (12 concepts × 2 regions), each deviation expressed as a fraction of the region’s value-added target. A draw is accepted only if it improves that scalar and the run completes all 100 periods.

Two things the scalar does not see, both relevant to the stability question:

  • It is a point snapshot at t = 100, so a config whose debt/GDP happens to pass through the target at t = 100 while still diverging after it scores well.
  • It does not contain the debt bound (min_t b_s > 0 and mean_t(b_s[t]/b_s[t-1] − 1) ≤ g), which is what “stable baseline” actually means. That bound is reported separately, and — for this seed — can never be met, because rates is not an instrument and rb = r_star + mu_b stays pinned at ~2.16% against g ≈ 1%, so (1+rb)/(1+g) > 1 throughout.

So the trajectory below is the fit path. The stability path is the 8 rates-instrument seeds launched alongside, which do report the bound per draw.

2. The trajectory

The objective falls 0.8094 → 0.0294 across 500 draws (11 accepted), then plateaus — the last ~150 draws move the incumbent only in the 4th decimal.

3. What the plateau means

The search has found the best point-fit its instrument set can reach — 0.0294 against the submitted reference of 0.019 and the sraffian starting point of 0.809. But because rates is absent, that config is still a diverging one: the debt bound is not in the objective and cannot be satisfied by the levers this seed is allowed to move. The plateau is the fit ceiling without stability, not a stable baseline.

The 8 seeds launched with taxes, propensities, rates are the experiment that decides whether the space contains a config that is both a good fit and stable; their per-draw debt_grow/g lines are the number this seed cannot produce.
